entries.title: Psalms 132:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Afflictions - All his sufferings for thy sake.

entries.title: Psalms 132:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Until - Until I have raised an house in which the ark may be put.

entries.title: Psalms 132:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: It - Of the ark. Ephratah - In the tribe of Ephraim, which was called also Ephratah. Found it - Afterwards we found it in Kirjath - jearim, which signifies a city of woods, in the territory whereof the ark was seated for twenty years.

entries.title: Psalms 132:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Tabernacles - Into his temple. Footstool - The ark, is often said to sit between the cherubim, which were above the ark.

entries.title: Psalms 132:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rest - Into thy resting place, the temple so called, Isa 66:1, where thou hast now a fixed habitation. The ark - The seat of thy powerful and glorious presence.

entries.title: Psalms 132:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: David's sake - In regard of thy promises vouchsafed to David. Turn not - Cast me not out of thy presence. Of - Of me whom thou hast anointed to be king over thy people.

entries.title: Psalms 132:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Salvation - With thy saving graces and blessings.

entries.title: Psalms 132:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: There - In Jerusalem. To bud - His power and glory to flourish. A lamp - A successor to continue for ever in his family, as this phrase is expounded 1Kings 11:36 15:4, and particularly one eminent and glorious light, namely, the Messiah.
